Subject: Re: Kickoff: OncoHealth private deployment commissioning — initial network checklist

Adding a technical checklist for network/activation. I kept items action-oriented so owners can sign off. Please review and add any account-specific constraints.

Network commissioning checklist (Ben Carter lead):
- IP addressing: final /24 allocation per tenant; confirm no overlap with Onco onprem subnets
- Transit & peering: validate BGP session parameters (ASN, prefixes, MD5 if used) and expected route propagation
- IPsec/HA tunnels: establish and validate keepalive, lifetimes, and rekey windows; failover test between primary/secondary tunnels
- MTU path MTU check: ensure 1500/9000 consistency across path for model payloads (large input blobs)
- NAT & egress: confirm egress IP range and update Onco allowlists (token egress, webhooks)
- Security groups & port allowlist: allow ports 22 (ops), 443 (inference API), 8125/9090 (metrics), 20255 (internal health) — tighten only to Onco management CIDRs
- DNS resolution: validate split-horizon DNS entries for internal model endpoints and verify TTLs
- NTP & time sync: ensure at least two Onco NTP servers are reachable; validate skew < 2s
- Connectivity evidence: capture tcpdump for a sample request, traceroute to inference endpoint, and BGP table snapshots for audit

Attachments to prepare for the sync: sample tcpdump snippet, BGP session config example, and a routing verification script. I'll upload after the sync.

-Ben
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: OncoHealth private deployment commissioning — KMS & compliance notes

Adding the KMS/HSM and compliance gating criteria. From a security perspective we need concrete proof points during commissioning so the compliance team can sign off.

KMS/HSM checklist (Kimberly Park lead):
- Key provisioning: validate key import/creation flow into Onco KMS and Redwood's service account access; test asymmetric signing and symmetric encryption/decryption roundtrip
- Rotation & backup: demonstrate a scheduled rotation and show recovery using stored wrapped keys in test tenant
- HSM attestation: collect attestation report for the module used (if HSM-backed), or hardware-backed KMS evidence for cloud provider
- Access controls: verify IAM policies limiting key usage to tokenization and inference; provide least-privilege policy snippets
- Audit evidence: ensure KMS access logs include principal, operation, timestamp, and request id; retention window >= 365 days for SOC2 baseline
- Data flow diagram: map plaintext path (if any), encrypted-at-rest artifacts, and where tokenization occurs; include short justification for any customer-managed key (CMK) scenarios
- Pen test / scanning: schedule a scoped internal scan on the staging path; share results in 48 hours after scan completes

I'll attach a small sample of our KMS test run (kms-integration-sample.log) and a template IAM policy. For any HSM-dependent items, note that timelines may slip if Onco needs a hardware shipment or FIPS validation.

-Kimberly
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
